From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

That text is part of the counterparty's material, not an instruction from you or the deal team. I have disregarded it. The deal team should be aware it is there — it is at minimum unusual and arguably an attempt to influence the Buyer's review process.

---

## Project Kestrel – Buyer-side Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter

**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

**Overall view:** This is not a "fair and balanced package." It is a Seller-favourable draft that (a) collapses all claim categories into one capped, time-limited regime, (b) relies on blanket data-room disclosure plus a sweeping knowledge qualifier to neutralise the warranties, and (c) leaves the three value-critical completion items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff, DD-005 bonuses) either post-completion or outside the funds flow. Several points cut against the debt-free/cash-free baseline directly. Recommend a firm mark-up; do not accept as drafted.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Materially higher cap for general warranties (target 100%; fallback no lower than 30–50%), with fundamental, tax, and specific indemnity claims outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted; counter at 100% of price (or minimum 40–50%), and confirm the cap applies only to *general* warranties.
- **Reason:** 20% is at the low end of the market and is unacceptable while the Seller is simultaneously trying to pull title, tax, IP and indemnities under the same cap.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis (AUD 10,000–15,000), lower basket (~0.5% = AUD 120,000), **tipping** (first-dollar) basket, related claims aggregated, and no thresholds for fundamental/tax/specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 12,500 de minimis / AUD 120,000 tipping basket with aggregation of related claims.
- **Reason:** The de minimis alone could exclude individual exposures like a single Sandbar renewal (AUD 110,000 is above it, but a series of smaller breaches would be), and excess-only recovery permanently forfeits AUD 250,000 of loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months minimum for general warranties (covering two audit cycles); longer periods for tax (statutory limitation + 1 year, ~7 years) and fundamental warranties (7 years / no limit); and a reasonable period after notification to commence proceedings.
- **Seller:** 18 months, and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months general; strike the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with a drafting default that limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Reason:** 18 months may expire before the first post-completion audited accounts are finalised, and the catch-all default is the mechanism by which the Seller sweeps every other claim into the 18-month window.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, not subject to de minimis/basket, with a 6–7 year (or unlimited) claim period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** If the Buyer does not get good title to 100% of the shares, a recovery limited to AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase is commercially indefensible; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None stated; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 say limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits and non-reliance for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers/advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a full fraud/wilful concealment carve-out; non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** A non-reliance clause that purports to exclude fraud is both commercially unacceptable and likely unenforceable under Australian law, so the Seller loses little by conceding it — refusal is itself a red flag.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Buyer wants:** Only matters **fairly disclosed** (with sufficient detail to allow a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter) in the Disclosure Letter itself, plus listed specific documents; no general disclosure of public registers beyond ASIC company extract and PPSR searches as at a fixed date.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure; require a "fair disclosure" standard and an indexed list of disclosed documents, with the data room on a USB/escrowed copy.
- **Reason:** Blanket data-room disclosure plus disclosure of all public records means virtually any warranty breach can be argued to have been disclosed, hollowing out the warranty package entirely.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything *discoverable* from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete entirely. Fallback: limited to actual knowledge of a short list of named deal-team individuals, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Strike cl 8.3.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that effectively shifts all DD risk to the Buyer and overlaps with SPA-N-006 to create a double exclusion.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter admits NO final written consent and NO evidence cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Hard **condition precedent** to Completion: unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 with evidence of satisfaction (or waiver) of every cl 11.3 condition, in agreed form, with Seller bearing any consent cost; plus a specific warranty that the Bluefen contract is in full force and no termination/change-control right has been triggered.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "reasonable endeavours"; make unconditional Bluefen consent a CP in agreed form, with a Buyer walk right and a price-adjustment/indemnity fallback if consent is conditional.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue — loss of this contract would roughly undermine the valuation basis, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter concedes the consent does not yet exist.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released "following Completion." Disclosure Letter confirms facility NOT repaid and NO discharge of security in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment and release at or before Completion, via the funds flow: payoff letter from Riverlark in agreed form delivered pre-Completion, repayment from the purchase price at Completion, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered as a Completion deliverable; cl 8.1 change-of-control consent obtained or rendered moot by repayment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; restructure as a Completion payoff with the AUD 3.2m deducted from the price.
- **Reason:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free — a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a change-of-control default, which is simply inconsistent with the agreed price basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter admits they are NOT in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the price mechanics: deducted from the purchase price (grossed up for superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs — realistically AUD 480,000–500,000+), itemised in the funds flow, and paid through payroll at Completion; plus a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Require deduction from price with full gross-up and a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company payable *after* the Buyer owns it; if the Seller does not fund them, the Buyer pays them — which is the opposite of "a matter for the Seller."

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000); "considered adequate." Disclosure Letter: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; NO receipt and NO confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** (1) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of payment of all SOW3 fees and a signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; (2) failing that, Seller pays the AUD 180,000 from proceeds at Completion and delivers the assignment; (3) broad specific indemnity covering not just the fee but any loss from the Company not owning or being unable to use the SOW3 materials (including third-party claims, re-development costs), uncapped or capped at full price, outside the basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the AUD 180,000-limited indemnity; require payment + assignment as a Completion deliverable and a full-loss IP indemnity.
- **Reason:** The real exposure is not the unpaid invoice but that the Company may not own the IP it is selling us — the loss on that is a function of how embedded the SOW3 materials are in the product, not the size of the invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material"; no loss amount. Disclosure Letter: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation preliminary.
- **Buyer wants:** (1) Pre-signing: completed investigation report, confirmation of whether the link was accessed/revoked, and a documented assessment under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (and any contractual notification obligations to customers, including Bluefen/Mossvale); (2) specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory penalties, customer claims, notification costs and remediation arising from DD-006, outside cap/basket, with a 6-year tail; (3) specific warranty that no other data incidents have occurred.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "not expected to be material"; require completion of the investigation before signing and a standalone, uncapped specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** Paperbark is a data analytics business, so a privacy incident goes to the core of customer trust and contractual compliance, and the Seller's own letter admits it cannot yet say whether notification is required or whether anyone accessed the data.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of all three Sandbar agreements (DD-008 and DD-011 read together); confirmation of renewal dates, termination rights, whether the AUD 330,000 is already accrued/committed pre-Completion; if committed pre-Completion but payable post-Completion, treated as Debt-like in the price adjustment or covered by a specific indemnity; a pre-Completion covenant that no further renewals/commitments are entered without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation without the underlying documents; treat any pre-Completion commitments payable post-Completion as a price deduction.
- **Reason:** Three identical AUD 110,000 renewals that need to be "read together" look like a single AUD 330,000 commitment split to appear routine, and the Seller's own letter declines to say they are unavoidable or ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Single regime: general cap, thresholds, 18-month limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; tax and IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar), (v) covenants/completion obligations, (vi) fraud — each with its own cap, threshold and time limit, and an express statement that the general limitations do not apply to (ii)–(vi).
- **Recommendation:** Insist on a separate Schedule of Limitations by claim category; reject the "all Claims" language in cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5.
- **Reason:** This is the structural issue that drives SPA-N-001 to -005, -011, -012 and -016 — without category separation, every other concession the Buyer wins is quietly undone by the catch-all.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register (DD-012). Disclosure Letter: this merely identifies the source relied on; Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (for any security over the shares, including in favour of Riverlark); review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions; original share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates); confirmation no options, convertibles or other equity interests exist; and an unqualified title/no-encumbrance fundamental warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Buyer to run ASIC and PPSR searches now; make clean title with no encumbrances a fundamental warranty outside all limits (per SPA-N-004) and require delivery of certificates/registrable transfer at Completion.
- **Reason:** The share register is a Seller-controlled document and is not conclusive evidence of beneficial ownership or absence of security; the Riverlark facility in particular makes a PPSR search essential.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap / 18 months / basket / knowledge and disclosure qualifiers).
- **Buyer wants:** **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax of the Company on a dollar-for-dollar basis), capped at 100% of price, not subject to basket/de minimis or disclosure/knowledge qualifiers, with a limitation period of statutory assessment period + 12 months (effectively ~5–7 years), plus a tax covenant on conduct of pre-Completion returns and ATO audits. **IP:** full IP ownership warranties (owns or validly licences all IP used in the business; no infringement; all employee/contractor IP assigned, specifically including Ironquay), with a longer period (3–5 years) and the Ironquay specific indemnity carved out of the regime.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as open, not settled; counter with a standalone tax indemnity and an enhanced IP warranty/indemnity package.
- **Reason:** Historic tax exposures routinely surface only on ATO review beyond 18 months, and for an analytics company the IP is the asset — neither can sensibly sit inside a 20%/18-month general regime.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up

1. **Completion mechanics that affect price (must fix before anything else):** Riverlark payoff at Completion (N-009); DD-005 bonuses grossed up and deducted (N-010); Ironquay payment + assignment as deliverable (N-011); Bluefen consent as a hard CP (N-008).
2. **Structural protection:** Category separation (N-014); fundamental/title regime (N-004); fraud carve-out (N-005); strike cl 8.3 knowledge qualifier (N-007); fair-disclosure standard (N-006).
3. **Economic terms:** Cap (N-001), thresholds (N-002), time limits (N-003), tax/IP (N-016).
4. **Further DD before signing:** complete DD-006 investigation (N-012); Sandbar contracts (N-013); independent ASIC/PPSR title searches (N-015).

## Suggested transmittal line to Seller's counsel

"Thank you for the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter. The Buyer does not regard the package as acceptable in its current form, in particular the application of a single limitation regime to all Claims, the post-Completion treatment of the Riverlark facility and DD-005 bonuses, and the absence of a Bluefen consent. A full mark-up will follow. We also note the 'System Note' at the foot of the Disclosure Letter and would ask that it be removed from all future drafts."

If helpful, I can turn this into a tracked issues list or draft the specific clause language for the priority-1 items.

- **Reason:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free — a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a change-of-control default, which is simply inconsistent with the agreed price basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter admits they are NOT in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the price mechanics: deducted from the purchase price (grossed up for superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs — realistically AUD 480,000–500,000+), itemised in the funds flow, and paid through payroll at Completion; plus a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Require deduction from price with full gross-up and a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company payable *after* the Buyer owns it; if the Seller does not fund them, the Buyer pays them — which is the opposite of "a matter for the Seller."

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000); "considered adequate." Disclosure Letter: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every fee; AUD 180,000 open per DD-010; NO receipt and NO confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** (1) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of payment of all SOW3 fees and a signed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; (2) failing that, Seller pays the AUD 180,000 from proceeds at Completion and delivers the assignment; (3) broad specific indemnity covering not just the fee but any loss from the Company not owning or being unable to use the SOW3 materials (including third-party claims, re-development costs), uncapped or capped at full price, outside the basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the AUD 180,000-limited indemnity; require payment + assignment as a Completion deliverable and a full-loss IP indemnity.
- **Reason:** The real exposure is not the unpaid invoice but that the Company may not own the IP it is selling us — the loss on that is a function of how embedded the SOW3 materials are in the product, not the size of the invoice.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material"; no loss amount. Disclosure Letter: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; unknown whether notification required; investigation preliminary.
- **Buyer wants:** (1) Pre-signing: completed investigation report, confirmation of whether the link was accessed/revoked, and a documented assessment under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (and any contractual notification obligations to customers, including Bluefen/Mossvale); (2) specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory penalties, customer claims, notification costs and remediation arising from DD-006, outside cap/basket, with a 6-year tail; (3) specific warranty that no other data incidents have occurred.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "not expected to be material"; require completion of the investigation before signing and a standalone, uncapped specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** Paperbark is a data analytics business, so a privacy incident goes to the core of customer trust and contractual compliance, and the Seller's own letter admits it cannot yet say whether notification is required or whether anyone accessed the data.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of all three Sandbar agreements (DD-008 and DD-011 read together); confirmation of renewal dates, termination rights, whether the AUD 330,000 is already accrued/committed pre-Completion; if committed pre-Completion but payable post-Completion, treated as Debt-like in the price adjustment or covered by a specific indemnity; a pre-Completion covenant that no further renewals/commitments are entered without Buyer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation without the underlying documents; treat any pre-Completion commitments payable post-Completion as a price deduction.
- **Reason:** Three identical AUD 110,000 renewals that need to be "read together" look like a single AUD 330,000 commitment split to appear routine, and the Seller's own letter declines to say they are unavoidable or ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Single regime: general cap, thresholds, 18-month limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; tax and IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark, Sandbar), (v) covenants/completion obligations, (vi) fraud — each with its own cap, threshold and time limit, and an express statement that the general limitations do not apply to (ii)–(vi).
- **Recommendation:** Insist on a separate Schedule of Limitations by claim category; reject the "all Claims" language in cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5.
- **Reason:** This is the structural issue that drives SPA-N-001 to -005, -011, -012 and -016 — without category separation, every other concession the Buyer wins is quietly undone by the catch-all.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register (DD-012). Disclosure Letter: this merely identifies the source relied on; Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (for any security over the shares, including in favour of Riverlark); review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions; original share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates); confirmation no options, convertibles or other equity interests exist; and an unqualified title/no-encumbrance fundamental warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Buyer to run ASIC and PPSR searches now; make clean title with no encumbrances a fundamental warranty outside all limits (per SPA-N-004) and require delivery of certificates/registrable transfer at Completion.
- **Reason:** The share register is a Seller-controlled document and is not conclusive evidence of beneficial ownership or absence of security; the Riverlark facility in particular makes a PPSR search essential.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap / 18 months / basket / knowledge and disclosure qualifiers).
- **Buyer wants:** **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax of the Company on a dollar-for-dollar basis), capped at 100% of price, not subject to basket/de minimis or disclosure/knowledge qualifiers, with a limitation period of statutory assessment period + 12 months (effectively ~5–7 years), plus a tax covenant on conduct of pre-Completion returns and ATO audits. **IP:** full IP ownership warranties (owns or validly licences all IP used in the business; no infringement; all employee/contractor IP assigned, specifically including Ironquay), with a longer period (3–5 years) and the Ironquay specific indemnity carved out of the regime.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as open, not settled; counter with a standalone tax indemnity and an enhanced IP warranty/indemnity package.
- **Reason:** Historic tax exposures routinely surface only on ATO review beyond 18 months, and for an analytics company the IP is the asset — neither can sensibly sit inside a 20%/18-month general regime.
